title: Suspect faces federal charges after explosive device found at Illinois ethanol plant | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

A suspect faces federal charges in connection with an explosive device found Friday at a central Illinois ethanol plant, according to a law enforcement official and an indictment in the case.

The suspect, identified by the indictment as Andrew Kozak, was arrested Monday morning, the official said.

Kozak is facing one count of threats regarding explosives and one count of interstate communications of a threat, according to jail and court records.

He is accused of threatening “to unlawfully damage and destroy a building and other real and personal property, by means of fire and an explosive.” He is also accused of sending “an email to BioUrja which indicated that explosive devices had been placed at the BioUrja facility,” according to the indictment.

The first count carries a maximum penalty of up to 10 years in prison and the second count carries a maximum penalty of up to five years in prison, US Attorney Gregory Gilmore said during a news conference Tuesday.

“Threats like those to the plant generate fear in our community and disrupt the daily lives of its members,” Gilmore said.

Kozak pleaded not guilty to the counts on Tuesday, and a detention hearing was scheduled for Friday, CNN affiliate WEEK reported.

CNN has reached out to his public defender for comment.

The discovery of the explosive device at BioUrja Renewables forced thousands of people to evacuate Peoria’s downtown area for about 24 hours as investigators searched the sprawling industrial facility to rule out any further threats.

The device did not explode, and no one was injured during the incident.

Because of the materials inside the facility, the device could have resulted in a one-mile blast radius if it had gone off, Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixonsaid Friday.

The FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives are involved in the investigation, the official told CNN, adding it was not yet clear whether the device was viable. There is no suspected nexus to foreign terrorism at this point, according to the official.

The FBI and other agencies involved went through evidence, served warrants, conducted interviews, and executed searches to identify Kozak, Ryan Presley, special agent in charge for the FBI’s Springfield field office, said during the news conference.

The arrest was “the result of a coordinated investigative effort, the rapid deployment of specialized resources from ATF’s bomb techs, certified explosive specialists, explosive detection canines, and intelligence personnel who have worked tirelessly around the clock since Friday to identify the offender allegedly responsible for this act,” John Maniff, assistant special agent in charge for the ATF’s Chicago field office, said.

The city of Peoria, located along the Illinois River 130 miles southwest of Chicago, has a population of more than 100,000. The BioUrja plant is near Peoria’s downtown and was built in the 1930s, according to the mayor.

“We’ve had a real-life Friday the 13th nightmare,” Mayor RitaAli told CNN’s Jessica Dean over the weekend.

“Thank you to our tireless law enforcement officers and first responders on call who worked around the clock to keep Peoria safe,” Gov. JB Pritzkerwrote on Facebook.

The evacuation order caused some downtown events to be canceled or rescheduled, including a minor league hockey game and a portion ofIllinois Comic Con.

This story has been updated with additional information.

CNN’s Laura Sharman, Martin Goillandeau, Eduardo Cuevas, Amanda Watts and Cindy Von Quednow contributed to this report.
